evidence.excerpt: A dataset of 214 production batches of three-layer LLDPE/mLLDPE/LLDPE cast films (40–80 µm) collected over 18 months from an industrial film producer was analysed to establish a statistical relationship between pinhole density (measured by electrical discharge imaging) and OTR. Pinhole density ranged from 0 to 8 pinholes/m² and OTR ranged from 1600 to 3100 cm³/(m²·day·bar). A linear regression model explained 61 % of OTR variance (R² = 0.61) using pinhole density as the sole predictor; inclusion of film thickness, extrusion speed and melt temperature raised R² to 0.79. Films with zero pinholes showed an OTR range of 1580–1980 cm³/(m²·day·bar), confirming that pinhole-free conditions alone do not guarantee low OTR. These findings are communicated to the production partner as a quality-control decision tool. The methodology is generic and applicable to other thin film geometries.
